features.text: The patient experienced shortness of breath and lightheadedness after a long bike ride over the weekend.
The shortness of breath and lightheadedness were intense, with the patient feeling like they couldn't catch their breath and were very light-headed.
The patient experienced mild chest pain that lasted about an hour and resolved on its own.
The chest pain was described as a mild ache, not sharp or pressure-like, and did not radiate to other areas.
The symptoms started during the bike ride and worsened as the ride continued, especially towards the end.
The chest discomfort was mild, intermittent, and not correlated with specific activities or positions during the ride.
The patient did not experience any prior episodes of chest discomfort or shortness of breath during physical exertion.
The patient has no history of syncope, palpitations, or chest discomfort during rest or with minimal exertion.
The patient has a history of migraines, managed with Imitrex and avoidance of bright lights.
The patient has a history of reflux, managed with Protonix.
The patient had cataract surgery about four and a half months ago.
The patient has no family history of heart disease.
The patient is taking Imitrex for migraines.
The patient is taking Protonix for reflux.
The patient has not had any prior cardiac evaluations such as ECG, stress test, or echocardiogram.
The patient has not experienced any recent changes in his exercise routine, including intensity, duration, or type of physical activity.
The patient had a cough with a cold in the last year and a half, but no wheezing or sputum production before the incident.
The patient experienced some wheezing after the incident, as noted by the doctor during the exam.
The patient has not had any pulmonary function tests or spirometry in the past.
The patient is willing to undergo pulmonary function tests to evaluate for asthma or bronchospasm.
